competency_fulfillment.rationale: Every sample directly assesses subtraction of numbers strictly below 1000 across varied standard and contextual scenarios. Problems such as "What is 510 − 382?" (seed 42), "244 − 150 = ___" (seed 44), "What is 823 − 659?" (seed 502), and "921 − 838 = 83. True or False?" (seed 501) rigorously evaluate multi-digit subtraction with regrouping, while items like "What is 71 − 60?" (seed 46) and "265 − 210 = 55. True or False?" (seed 85) assess subtraction without regrouping.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The sample set comprehensively covers all dimensions of the competency: subtraction without regrouping (e.g., "There are 765 baskets on the table. Moses takes away 110 baskets. How many baskets are left on the table?" - seed 601), single and double regrouping across tens and hundreds (e.g., "What is 930 − 408?" - seed 600, "What is 270 − 247?" - seed 602), identity and boundary cases (e.g., "What is 11 − 0?" - seed 43, "What is 416 − 0?" - seed 604, "1 − 1 = ___" - seed 603), number line and counting back representations ("The dot is at 116 and it moves backward 20 numbers. Starting from 116, just count back 20 numbers. Which number will the dot land on?" - seed 50), part-whole relations ("The total is 380 and one part is 210. What is the other part?" - seed 55), and error analysis ("Ana solved: "152 − 150 = ___". Ana says the missing number is 302. Is Ana correct?" - seed 51).

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The language complexity, reading burden, and syntactic structure are well-calibrated for Grade 2 Quarter 2 learners. Real-world contexts are simple and concrete (e.g., baskets on a table in seed 601), counting backward scaffolding is explicitly phrased ("Starting from 28, just count back 15 numbers. Which number will the dot land on?" - seed 605), and distractors target genuine arithmetic errors such as addition instead of subtraction (e.g., 892 in seed 42) or off-by-one errors without introducing excessive cognitive load.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: There is a rich variety of question formats represented in the packet, including standard multiple choice ('mcq', e.g., "What is 510 − 382?"), fill-in-the-blank/equation cloze ('cloze', e.g., "30 − 29 = ___"), number-line/contextual multiple choice ('read_mcq', e.g., "The dot is at 116 and it moves backward 20 numbers. Starting from 116, just count back 20 numbers. Which number will the dot land on?"), part-whole prompts ('read_fill_in_blank', e.g., "The total is 591 and one part is 487. What is the other part?"), verification statements ('true_false', e.g., "921 − 838 = 83. True or False?"), and conceptual misconception checking ('error_detect', e.g., "Ana solved: "152 − 150 = ___". Ana says the missing number is 302. Is Ana correct?").

competency_alignment.rationale: All problems strictly remain within the scope of Grade 2 Quarter 2 subtraction. All minuends and subtrahends are whole numbers under 1000, and differences are non-negative whole numbers (≥ 0). No advanced operations, negative numbers, or unintroduced concepts are included, ensuring 100% alignment with MATATAG node mat_g2_na_q2_6.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Number magnitude strictly adheres to the 'less than 1000' boundary. The sample spans single-digit operations ("1 − 1 = ___"), two-digit numbers ("30 − 29 = ___", "What is 71 − 60?"), and large three-digit minuends extending up to 930 ("What is 930 − 408?") and 921 ("921 − 838 = 83. True or False?"), providing balanced scale representation across the entire allowable range.
